findings.note: Sheet 012, row 6. Clean shows the cartridge with a WHITE inner label panel carrying legible multi-line text ('NES / SUPER MARIO') plus a dark border frame and dark NINTENDO footer bar. In the risograph tile the ENTIRE cartridge — including the white inner label panel — is flooded with solid dark grey ink, so the white paper region is shaded and the SUPER MARIO text is buried into the mass (white-shaded -> detail-lost). Confirmed at 4x zoom against clean. This is ISOLATED, not blanket risograph behavior: risograph on ampCombo (s000 r6, white slatted body) and cardBinder (s012 r10, white card pockets) correctly KEEP their enclosed white regions as paper, and bandTshirt/boardingPass riso keep their labels legible. So the cartridge's nested white label panel is wrongly being treated as fillable instead of as paper.
findings.researchedFix: Two established fixes apply. (1) Duotone/risograph luminance-preservation: a faithful risograph/duotone mapping must scale each region's tone to lie between PAPER color and INK color according to source luminance, so high-luminance (white/paper) regions map to paper and receive no ink; only darker source regions take the spot ink. The cartridge's high-luminance inner label should map to paper, matching how cel-shading quantizes lighting to discrete shades while leaving the lightest band un-inked. (2) SVG fill-rule: when a path has an enclosed inner region (the white label nested inside the cartridge outline), fill-rule='nonzero' (the default) fills the entire shape including the inner 'hole', whereas fill-rule='evenodd' leaves the nested inner region empty — 'choosing the wrong fill rule could accidentally fill regions (like a background area) that should remain empty.' Set fill-rule:evenodd (or ensure the riso ink layer respects var(--dir-bg)/none/transparent paper fills and never overrides them) so the inner label stays paper.
findings.citation: Duotone luminance preservation: US Patent 5,982,924 'Method and system for reproducing color images as duotones' (image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/5982924) — luminance scaled to lie between paper color and black ink. Cel/threshold quantization: Cel shading, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cel_shading. SVG fill-rule fix: 'Understanding the SVG fill-rule Property', sitepoint.com/understanding-svg-fill-rule-property/ and MDN fill-rule, developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Attribute/fill-rule (even-odd leaves nested regions empty; wrong rule accidentally fills regions that should remain empty).

findings.note: Clean shows THREE domino tiles stacked vertically, each with pip dots. Under bold-ink only ONE tile (the top one) renders; the lower two tiles are entirely dropped. Same failure across the whole solid/textured-fill family on this row: rough-handdrawn, sketchy, bold-ink, wet-ink, charcoal, stipple ALL collapse to a single tile. The pure-outline / texture-overlay styles (risograph, newsprint, outline-only, wireframe) correctly render all three. Pattern = the three tiles are disjoint subpaths in one compound geometry, and the hand-style solid/hachure fill only resolves the first subpath, dropping the rest. bold-ink is the clearest single representative (crisp single tile, two missing).
findings.researchedFix: Root cause is rough.js filling compound/disjoint subpaths under one winding rule with the fill limited to the first subpath / canvas bounds (hachure cutoff). Fix: do NOT pass the multi-tile geometry as one compound path to rough.js for solid/hachure fill styles; iterate and call the rough fill per-subpath (split the path on each M...Z and roughen+fill each tile separately, then composite). This matches the rough.js maintainer guidance to draw separate shapes rather than one path with multiple regions.
findings.citation: https://github.com/rough-stuff/rough/issues/167 (fill always non-zero / multi-region path fill) and https://github.com/rough-stuff/rough/issues/65 (Hachure fill cutoff in SVG-Path polygons)

findings.note: Clean shows a tin whose body panel is light gray containing a WHITE circle with a '+' emblem and a small label below. Under risograph the inner panel is filled a flat dark gray and the white circle+plus emblem is buried into a featureless dark mass (only a faint dot survives) — the white emblem region (a hole/cutout) got shaded over, losing the central detail. Newsprint on the same row preserves the white circle+emblem, so the failure is risograph-specific.
findings.researchedFix: Cause is rough.js filling the path with the non-zero fill-rule so the inner emblem subpath (which should be a hole / unfilled cutout) is filled solid instead of left as paper. Fix: render the emblem cutout as its OWN reversed subpath or as a separate top layer drawn AFTER the body fill (re-stamp the white circle+plus over the risograph fill), since rough.js does not honor fill-rule='evenodd' for holes; equivalently subtract the inner region by reversing its winding before handing the path to rough.js.
findings.citation: https://github.com/rough-stuff/rough/issues/167 (Filling a path is always done with non-zero fill-rule — holes get filled); fill-rule/holes background: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/fill-rule

findings.note: Clean = solid-black canton (top-left) + 3 solid-black horizontal stripes. rough-handdrawn renders the canton as an EMPTY white box and the dark stripes as faint hatch outlines, so the dark/light contrast that defines the flag is lost. Fill-capable styles (wet-ink, charcoal, stipple, risograph, newsprint) all preserve the dark regions, confirming this is a stroke-only-style fill failure, not expected behavior. (outline-only/wireframe legitimately drop fill, not flagged.)
findings.researchedFix: Rough.js only renders hachure/fill when a fill COLOR is passed to the drawable; with no fill set the shape is outlined only. Fix: route the region's solid fill color into the Rough.js options (fill: <regionColor>, fillStyle 'hachure' or 'solid' for dark regions) so dark fills are hatched/filled instead of dropped. Per StudyRaid: the fill option must be set with a color value for hachure hatching to appear; without it the shape only shows the outline with transparent fill and no hatching.

findings.note: Same root cause as rough-handdrawn but more severe: the solid-black canton + stripes are reduced to thin sketchy outlines with near-zero shading, so the flag reads as a blank grid. Dark regions go light/empty.
findings.researchedFix: Same as flagPanel/rough-handdrawn: pass the region fill color into Rough.js so the solid-dark canton and stripes get a hachure/solid fill instead of outline-only. Use fillStyle 'solid' (or dense hachure with small hachureGap) for regions whose source luminance is near-black so they read dark.

findings.note: Clean canton is solid black; bold-ink draws it as an empty white box with only a bold outline, and the dark stripes become empty outlined bands. The bold-ink style strokes paths but never fills the solid-dark regions, so all dark fills are dropped to white.
findings.researchedFix: Same fix family: ensure the dark fill regions receive a Rough.js fill color (fillStyle 'solid' for near-black regions); bold-ink should keep its heavy stroke but ADD a solid/dense-hachure fill driven by source luminance so dark canton/stripes don't read as empty.

findings.note: Clean = dark frame around a WHITE mat with a distinct dark canvas square + text lines. risograph fills the entire object (mat included) with a uniform dark-gray mass, burying the canvas square and text. The light mat region is shaded dark. All other fill styles (wet-ink, charcoal, stipple, newsprint) keep the mat light, so this is risograph-specific posterization pushing the light mat below the dark cutoff.
findings.researchedFix: risograph posterize uses feComponentTransfer type='discrete' tableValues; the band breakpoints are clipping light/white values into the dark band. Fix: anchor the top tableValues entry to 1 (preserve highlights) so light mat maps to paper not ink, and/or raise the discrete step so near-white stays in the lightest band. Codrops/Sudonull posterize-with-feComponentTransfer is the canonical pattern.

findings.note: Clean = black frame around a WHITE poster interior (title text) + dark bottom credit band. risograph fills the white interior dark gray; the title is nearly illegible and the object is one dark mass with a faint white outline rect. charcoal/newsprint keep the interior white, confirming a risograph-only light-region-clipped-to-dark issue.
findings.researchedFix: Same as framedCanvas/risograph: correct the feComponentTransfer discrete tableValues so the highest input band maps to paper (1.0) and white interior is preserved; the current band table collapses mid/high luminance into the ink band. Preserve highlights by anchoring the top table entry.

findings.note: Clean = dark photo field with a clear WHITE runner-silhouette figure + light top text band. risograph keeps the dark field (correct) but buries the white figure -- only two tiny white tick-marks (feet) survive. charcoal and newsprint both retain the full white figure, so risograph posterization is collapsing the light figure into the surrounding dark band (loss of the light-on-dark detail).
findings.researchedFix: Posterize banding is merging the figure's light luminance into the dark field. Fix: increase the number of discrete bands (more tableValues steps) and/or add a dedicated high band so the figure's brightness lands in a lighter band than the photo field; per W3C, type='discrete' nValues create n bands -- too few bands erases mid/high detail. Keep at least one light band above the figure luminance.

findings.note: Clean = upright bottle with a FLAT bottom and rounded shoulder. rough-handdrawn collapses the flat base + lower body into a converging downward SPIKE -- the rectangular base is lost and the silhouette becomes a tapered point. risograph/newsprint/outline/wireframe keep the correct flat-bottom bottle, so this is path-roughening breaking the closed bottle path.
findings.researchedFix: Known Rough.js behavior: high roughness breaks/distorts closed paths (GitHub issue #162 'Path has been break apart when applying roughness=2'). Fix: lower roughness/maxRandomnessOffset for this path, lower bowing, and/or ensure the bottle outline is a single properly-closed path (close with 'Z' so base corners aren't pulled to a point). Reduce per-segment randomness on long near-vertical edges so the base stays flat.

findings.note: Same as rough-handdrawn: the flat bottle base becomes a sharp downward point and the body warps; the bottle silhouette is no longer readable as a flat-bottomed bottle.
findings.researchedFix: Same fix: reduce roughness/maxRandomnessOffset and ensure the path is explicitly closed (Z) so corners aren't pulled into a spike; clamp randomness on the base segment.

findings.note: Flat bottom rendered as a pointed spike; lower body warped. Same path-distortion as rough/sketchy, just with a heavier stroke.
findings.researchedFix: Same: lower roughness, close the path (Z), clamp base-segment randomness so the flat base survives the roughening.

findings.note: Bottle base distorted into a converging point and body skewed vs Clean's flat-bottom upright bottle. Same closed-path roughening failure.
findings.researchedFix: Same: reduce roughness/maxRandomnessOffset, ensure closed (Z) path, clamp base randomness.

findings.note: Flat-bottom bottle rendered as a tapered spike with warped body. Same path-distortion as the other roughened styles.
findings.researchedFix: Same: reduce roughness/maxRandomnessOffset, close the path (Z), clamp randomness on the base edge.

findings.note: Flat bottle base collapses to a point and body warps, same as the other stroke-roughened styles; silhouette no longer reads as a flat-bottomed bottle.
findings.researchedFix: Same: reduce roughness/maxRandomnessOffset, ensure the outline path is closed (Z), clamp base-segment randomness.

findings.note: Clean tile shows a full pyramid stack of ~10 LaCroix cans (4-3-2-1 triangle). In rough-handdrawn the entire multi-can stack collapses to a single tiny ~1-2 cell dark box at top-center, with only a faint partial 4th can dropping out below the edge. The whole composition is lost vs Clean. risograph/newsprint/outline-only/wireframe correctly preserve the full pyramid, so the geometry exists; the sketchy pass collapses it. Same failure also affects sketchy, bold-ink, wet-ink, charcoal, stipple in this row.
findings.researchedFix: This is the classic rough.js multi-element / compound-path collapse: a drawing made of many disconnected subpaths (the 10 can shapes) is being passed through one sketchy pass and reduced to a single bounding mass. Fix: flatten transforms and split the composition into its individual subpaths/elements, then run the sketchy/rough transform per-subpath rather than on the grouped whole. rough.js itself normalizes each subpath into separate Move/Line/Cubic OpSets, so feeding it pre-split subpaths (via an SVG flattener that handles all path commands) renders every can. See shihn.ca rough.js algorithm notes (normalizes paths into per-subpath Move/Line/Cubic OpSets) and Flatten.js / svg-path-commander for splitting+normalizing subpaths before the sketchy filter.

findings.note: Same collapse as rough-handdrawn: the 10-can pyramid renders as a single small box outline instead of the full stack. Detail of the multi-can composition is lost vs Clean.
findings.researchedFix: Same fix family: split the grouped multi-can drawing into its subpaths/elements and apply the sketchy transform per-subpath; flatten transforms first so each can keeps its own placement.

findings.note: Pyramid collapses to a single small filled box; the 10-can stack is gone vs Clean.
findings.researchedFix: Render the composition per-subpath instead of as one grouped shape; flatten/normalize subpaths before the bold-ink stroke pass so each can is drawn.

findings.note: Pyramid collapses to a single dark filled box; multi-can detail lost vs Clean.
findings.researchedFix: Split the grouped drawing into individual can subpaths and apply the wet-ink fill/stroke per-subpath after flattening transforms.

findings.note: Pyramid collapses to a single small smudged box; the can stack is not rendered vs Clean.
findings.researchedFix: Apply the charcoal transform per-subpath on the flattened/normalized can subpaths rather than on the grouped composition.

findings.note: Pyramid collapses to a single small box; the multi-can stack is lost vs Clean. (risograph/newsprint/outline-only/wireframe in the same row preserve the full pyramid, confirming the geometry is present and the collapse is style-pass-specific.)
findings.researchedFix: Run the stipple fill per-subpath on the split/normalized can subpaths; flatten transforms first so each can is stippled in place instead of one collapsed region.

findings.note: Clean shows a DARK passport cover carrying light knockout detail (legible 'UNITED STATES OF AMERICA' text + circular emblem) overlapping a lighter document page peeking out at right. The newsprint variant collapses the entire dark cover into a uniform halftone dot field: the white text, the emblem, and the cover-vs-document layering all vanish into one featureless dot rectangle. Verified at full-crop resolution (/tmp/c108_passdoc_clean.png vs /tmp/c108_passdoc_newsprint.png). The other styles handle this same dark region correctly — risograph (/tmp/c108_passdoc_risograph.png) and bold-ink (/tmp/c108_passdoc_bold.png) both keep the text, emblem, and document-behind readable — which isolates the failure to newsprint's flat dot fill. Root cause: newsprint applies a uniform dot screen across the whole dark silhouette instead of modulating dot coverage by source luminance, so light knockout interior detail is destroyed.
findings.researchedFix: Drive newsprint halftone dot coverage from the SOURCE pixel luminance (clustered-dot / ordered dither), the canonical halftone model: dark source -> large merged dots (stays dark), light/knockout source -> small-or-no dots (stays light), so interior white text/emblem survive. This is exactly how GIMP's Newsprint filter works — it requires a grayscale luminance input and renders a clustered-dot dither whose dot size tracks tone, rather than a flat fill over the silhouette. Implement by sampling the rasterized object luminance (or treating explicit fill-vs-knockout regions distinctly) and mapping it to dot radius/threshold per cell.
findings.citation: GIMP Newsprint filter docs (clustered-dot dither, grayscale luminance input, Cell-size dot modulation): https://docs.gimp.org/2.10/en/gimp-filter-newsprint.html ; ordered dithering / threshold-by-luminance per-cell model: https://users.ece.utexas.edu/~bevans/projects/halftoning/methods.html

findings.note: Milder instance of the same root cause. Clean shows a DARK 'NINTENDO POWER' header banner with legible light text plus a dark center circle (/tmp/c108_powermag_clean.png). In newsprint the header banner becomes a flat halftone dot strip and the 'NINTENDO POWER' text is no longer readable, buried in the dot field (/tmp/c108_powermag_newsprint.png). Overall structure (header band + center disc + frame) is still recognizable, so this is a partial detail-loss rather than a full collapse — but the white knockout text on the dark banner is lost, same failure mode as passportDocument. Light-region objects under newsprint elsewhere (e.g. passport row10 light cover) render faithfully, confirming the problem is specific to newsprint over dark knockout-bearing fills.
findings.researchedFix: Same fix as passportDocument: make newsprint dot coverage a function of source luminance so the dark banner stays dark while its light text knockout produces little/no dot coverage and remains legible. Use a luminance-thresholded clustered-dot dither per cell (GIMP Newsprint model) instead of a uniform dot fill applied to the whole dark region.
findings.citation: GIMP Newsprint filter docs (luminance-driven clustered-dot halftone): https://docs.gimp.org/2.10/en/gimp-filter-newsprint.html ; halftoning methods (ordered/threshold dither preserves tone): https://users.ece.utexas.edu/~bevans/projects/halftoning/methods.html

findings.note: Clean is a SOLID DARK card with white 'DDW' logo + small caption. rough-handdrawn renders only an empty light outlined rectangle — the dark fill is dropped and the white-on-dark logo/caption vanish entirely. wet-ink and charcoal (same row) correctly keep the dark block, proving the dark region exists in source; the line-style preset is emitting it stroke-only with no fill.
findings.researchedFix: In Rough.js, a closed dark-filled region must be drawn with fill:<darkInk> + fillStyle:'solid' (true solid blocks) rather than stroke-only; the path must be closed with Z so fill applies. For NPR correctness, preserve the region's tonal value via a Tonal Art Map so a dark region keeps high hatch density and never collapses to empty.

findings.note: Same row as above: sketchy renders an empty light outlined rectangle, dropping the solid-dark card fill and the white 'DDW' logo + caption. wet-ink/charcoal in the same row keep the dark block.
findings.researchedFix: Map the solid-dark fill to Rough.js fillStyle:'solid' (or dense cross-hatch with small hachureGap + heavier fillWeight) with a closed Z path so the dark tone is preserved instead of dropped.

findings.note: Same row: bold-ink draws a heavy empty outlined rectangle with no interior fill — the dark card and white logo/caption are dropped. wet-ink/charcoal keep them.
findings.researchedFix: bold-ink should still carry fill:<darkInk> with fillStyle:'solid' on the closed region; thickening the stroke alone leaves the interior empty. Preserve tonal value via TAM-style dense fill.
findings.citation: Rough.js fill options https://github.com/rough-stuff/rough ; Tonal Art Maps https://gfx.cs.princeton.edu/proj/sg05lines/course7-4-npr.pdf

findings.note: Clean shows a fully-inked circular buckle disc carrying a white 'W' logo. rough-handdrawn renders the disc as a hollow outline only — the dark fill is dropped and the 'W' negative-space mark vanishes. This is a regression, not by-design: charcoal/stipple/risograph/bold-ink/wet-ink all retain the dark disc + W; only the sketch-family paths drop it. The buckle is the object's focal dark element.
findings.researchedFix: rough.js (the hand-drawn engine class these styles derive from) preserves region fills only when the path is closed AND a fill+fillStyle are passed; outline-only output means fillStyle isn't propagated to the filled subpath. Fix: for ink/sketch styles, set fillStyle:'solid' (or 'hachure') with the source fill color on closed filled regions instead of stroking outline-only. rough.js supports hachure/solid/zigzag/cross-hatch/dots fill styles.
findings.citation: https://github.com/rough-stuff/rough (README: fill + fillStyle on closed paths; outline-only occurs when fill not propagated); https://roughjs.com/

findings.note: Same failure as rough-handdrawn: the solid dark buckle disc and its white 'W' mark are reduced to a hollow outline. sketchy is an ink style (not outline-only/wireframe), so the dark region should be preserved as it is in charcoal/stipple/risograph.
findings.researchedFix: Propagate fill+fillStyle to the closed buckle subpath in the sketchy renderer (rough.js fillStyle:'hachure' or 'solid'); do not strip the fill to outline. Outline-only and wireframe legitimately drop fills — sketchy should not.
findings.citation: https://github.com/rough-stuff/rough (fillStyle options: hachure, solid, cross-hatch); https://roughjs.com/

findings.note: newsprint fills the buckle disc with a dense uniform halftone, but the white 'W' logo (negative space in clean) is completely buried under the dot mass — the mark is gone, leaving a featureless halftone blob.
findings.researchedFix: Halftone should be threshold-driven from the source luminance and must keep negative-space regions (where source is light) dot-free. Mask the halftone with the source white/light areas before screening so the 'W' stays as un-dotted paper, varying dot radius with reflectance rather than flooding the whole disc.
findings.citation: https://weber.itn.liu.se/~stegu/webglshadertutorial/shadertutorial.html (vary dot radius/threshold by reflectance so white area stays proportional, preserving light/negative-space regions)

findings.note: Clean ticket has crisp 'RINGSIDE' text and a stub digit. newsprint overlays a halftone fill + dashed border that fades the body text into the dot field and nearly erases the stub digit — interior text is no longer legible.
findings.researchedFix: Exclude text/label sub-regions from the halftone screen (treat as light/negative space, dot-free) or apply halftone only to fill regions, keeping text strokes as solid ink overprint above the screen.
findings.citation: https://weber.itn.liu.se/~stegu/webglshadertutorial/shadertutorial.html (threshold proportional to reflectance keeps light areas open; screen fills, not detail strokes)

findings.note: Clean has a dark text bar and a solid dark button (bottom-right) plus content lines inside a browser window. newsprint reduces all interior content to a faint uniform halftone — the dark bar and the dark button essentially disappear (dark regions screened to near-light), so the UI structure is lost.
findings.researchedFix: Drive halftone dot size from source luminance: dark source regions (bar, button) must produce large/merged dots (near-solid), not faint dots. Current output applies a uniform light screen regardless of source darkness. Map threshold to per-pixel source value.

findings.note: rod tiles reveal a full face (two eyes + smile + two ears); extrude collapses it into a featureless dark glossy oval. auto also buries the face. inflate/solid keep eyes+smile. The face is the object's whole identity and it vanishes under extrude/auto.
findings.researchedFix: Don't bury 2D interior marks under a flat extruded cap. Treat interior line features as engraving: bake the clean SVG line layer into a grayscale displacement/bump map and apply to the extruded cap so eyes/smile read as recessed relief (white=high, black=low). Displacement mapping is the established technique for engravings/reliefs 'especially when silhouettes and edge breaks are relevant.'

findings.note: rod reveals a card with a championship-belt/figure icon inside a bordered frame; extrude and auto render a plain solid dark card slab with zero interior detail. inflate/solid keep the icon. Classic multi-feature flat drawing buried by the extrude cap.

Established displacement-map workflow for adding engraved/interior features to an extruded 2D base form without re-modeling each feature.

findings.note: rod/auto/inflate/solid all keep the open headband arc + two distinct earcups with center holes. extrude fills the entire open band-and-earcup negative space into one solid dark featureless mass; the defining open-arc topology is destroyed. inflate/solid keep the structure.

Open paths have no fill in three.js, so the band must be a closed shape WITH holes, with correct EVENODD/NONZERO winding, or the loader fills/inverts the hole. Known SVGLoader hole/winding pitfall.

Use SVGLoader.createShapes and put the inner circle into Shape.holes with correct winding (EVENODD vs NONZERO) so the band extrudes as an annulus. This is the documented circle-with-hole/donut SVGLoader case that loads filled/inverted if winding/holes aren't handled.

findings.note: CLEAN is a thin, open wavy stroke with zero filled area (dk 0.00; sampled CLEAN tile min pixel=106, true-black fraction=0.0). The extrude mode treats this open polyline as a closed fillable region and triangulates its interior into a solid black mass (extrude tile min pixel=24, ~3.9% true-black coverage), producing two irregular filled lumps instead of a thin 3D stroke. The line character of the noodle is destroyed. auto and rod render it as a faithful thin line; inflate and solid render it correctly as a thin puffy tube along the curve — so only extrude fails. Root cause: open paths are being sent through the extrude (closed-shape) pipeline.
findings.researchedFix: Detect open vs closed paths before choosing the 3D primitive. ExtrudeGeometry is designed only for closed 2D shapes — it fills/triangulates the interior, so feeding it an open polyline yields a filled-blob silhouette (a documented limitation). For open polylines/strokes route to a tube/ribbon along the curve (three.js TubeGeometry, which wraps a constant-radius tube along any 3D curve) — the same approach the inflate/solid modes already use here correctly. Equivalently, in CAD terms a closed polyline extrudes to a solid while an open polyline does not render as a solid and must instead be used as a sweep PATH or have its stroke expanded first. Concretely: if path.isClosed === false (or first point != last point), skip ExtrudeGeometry and build a TubeGeometry from a CatmullRomCurve3 of the polyline points; reserve ExtrudeGeometry for closed contours only.

findings.variant: extrude (extrude-q35 and extrude-q315; auto-q35/auto-q315 follow extrude and show the same defect)
findings.note: The Clean tile is a slim bottle: narrow neck, gentle shoulder, then a roughly constant-width straight-walled cylindrical body. The rod-q35/q315 (outline trace) and solid-q35/q315 (mesh) modes reproduce this faithfully — proper neck + straight body + 'M' label. But extrude-q35/q315 (and auto, which mirrors extrude) widen the lower body into a triangular FLARE, rendering the bottle as a wide spatula/paddle instead of a cylinder. The straight-walled body silhouette is mis-derived only in the extrude path; the same object is correct in rod and solid, so this is specific to the extrude-mode contour/triangulation, not the source SVG. Verified at 2x and 3x zoom.
findings.researchedFix: The flare is a contour-preservation/triangulation defect in the extrude path, not a bevel artifact (no bevel offset would convert a straight wall into a flare). Fix family: feed the extrusion the faithful closed contour via SVGLoader.toShapes() and let ShapeUtils.triangulateShape handle it with correct outer-CW/hole-CCW winding so the concave straight-walled profile is preserved rather than collapsed toward a convex hull — the same triangulation/winding discipline the solid+rod paths already use (their output is correct). three.js docs note shape triangulation must respect winding order for proper outline preservation, and ExtrudeGeometry depends on that contour. If a hull/simplification step is being applied before extrusion, remove it so extrude consumes the same contour as solid. Also confirm bevelOffset/bevelSize are not silently inflating the base (use negative bevelOffset = -bevelSize if bevel is on).

findings.note: Clean is a near-solid dark medal (dk 0.91): ribbon/loop + filled disc. findings.researchedFix: Drive the rod/skeleton geometry from the FILLED region's medial axis (grassfire/medial-axis transform of the filled area), not from the path stroke, so a dk~0.91 closed fill produces solid mass. Honor SVG fill-rule (nonzero/evenodd) when deciding what is interior before generating geometry. Cite: Carnegie Mellon Skeletonization (medial axis from filled discretized objects) and W3C SVG painting/fill-rule spec.
